bullets.title: PLTR surges 27% on fifth straight triple play; Deutsche Bank upgrades to Buy at $200
bullets.body: Palantir jumped 27% on Q2 results showing $1.94B revenue, +93% YoY—its 12th consecutive quarter of accelerating growth. Bespoke notes it's the only Russell 1000 stock that has never moved less than 5% on earnings, having now posted five straight triple plays (eight in nine quarters). Deutsche Bank upgraded to Buy with a $200 price target as AI sovereignty narrative gains traction.

bullets.title: FCC drafts ban on Chinese optical transceivers; AAOI +18%, LITE +7%, COHR and photonics stack rally
bullets.body: The FCC is drafting a rule to block imports of new Chinese optical transceiver models used in AI data centers. Fintwit bulls argue the ban benefits U.S. suppliers: AAOI jumped 18% as sole domestic alternative, LITE surged 7% as the only supplier of 200Gbps EMLs critical to Nvidia GB200 and Google TPUv7, COHR has a $5.81B backlog through 2027 and received a $2B NVDA strategic investment, and CIEN holds ~50% North American optical networking share with a $7.8B backlog. One account framed the ban as 'The Trump administration is telling you exactly what to invest in.'

bullets.title: AXTI split: bulls see InP permit leverage, bears fear China export controls
bullets.body: AXTI fell sharply on news of potential China InP export restrictions, then bounced 12% off lows. Bulls argue AXTI is actually in a 'powerful negotiating position' because the U.S. needs InP substrate supply easing and the Trump administration is aware—making this a potential bullish catalyst if rules relax. Bears counter that if China restricts InP exports, AXTI loses its primary supply chain advantage. One account noted AXTI supplies InP substrates to LITE, giving it upfront funding and long-term demand visibility.

bullets.title: NVDA: HBM4 alternative evaluation underway for Rubin Ultra; Blackwell GPUs at $2/hr for AI startups
bullets.body: Trendforce reports Nvidia has been evaluating 8-Hi HBM4e, 12-Hi HBM4, and 8-Hi HBM4 alternatives for Rubin Ultra since early Q3 2026 due to supply constraints and HBM4e validation risks, with a 2027 DRAM shortage expected to limit memory availability. Separately, Gavin Baker disclosed a top-tier AI startup renting Blackwell clusters at mid-$2 per GPU hour—pricing that implies compressed hyperscaler utilization economics. A separate analyst noted game theory supports durability of memory LTAs and Nvidia may derive significant revenue from cloud revenue-share arrangements.

bullets.title: Gamma squeeze and negative gamma at 6th-largest on record as S&P hits ATH
bullets.body: Nomura's McElligott described 'absolute scenes' with negative gamma from options and leveraged ETF rebalancing at the 6th largest print on record, driving a 'vol up, spot up' dynamic. A separate account noted 'massive demand for short-dated index upside this week' (primarily S&P and Nasdaq) following July de-risking, with $30M+ in OTM SPY calls and a $2.7M QQQ call at a 900 strike observed. QQQ rose 9% since last Wednesday, nearly exiting correction territory, while 70% of S&P 500 stocks are above their 200-day moving averages—the highest level in a year.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz: Iran signals mine-clearing flexibility; oil plunges 5.7%; reopening still uncertain
bullets.body: Iran is considering allowing European nations to clear mines in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran-Oman talks described as 'positive at technical and political levels.' Bessent suggested a deal could materialize by Tuesday or Wednesday. However, Rubio cautioned 'nothing final,' Nomura's McElligott called it 'v33' of the ceasefire narrative (implying repeated failed attempts), and shipping analysts note fewer than 10 ships in current traffic patterns. Oil dropped 5.7% to below $76/bbl on the news.

bullets.title: MRVL breaks $200; ALAB PCIe switch thesis articulated vs. AVGO and MRVL
bullets.body: MRVL broke above $200 and was cited as 'one of the hottest semiconductor stocks lately.' A separate detailed thread analyzed the transition from PCIe retimers to switches, comparing ALAB, Broadcom, and Marvell offerings for scale-up AI infrastructure with AWS warrant dynamics as a key consideration.

bullets.title: MU pullback called buying opportunity by BofA; $707 post-market flagged as potential bottom
bullets.body: BofA reiterated its Buy rating on Micron with a $1,550 price target, calling the recent selloff an 'enhanced buying opportunity' as memory pricing normalizes 2027–2028. Separately, one account noted MU's $707 post-market price 'appears to mark the bottom,' emphasizing MU's non-commodity positioning in HBM. Trendforce also flagged a 2027 DRAM shortage supporting the memory bull case.

bullets.title: CRWV +20% on Indonesia data center expansion; 360MW across three facilities
bullets.body: CoreWeave announced expansion into Indonesia with three new data centers totaling 360 megawatts, driven by growing demand for localized AI compute capacity. Stock surged 20% on the announcement with facilities expected to come online in 2028.

bullets.title: NVDA launches Alpamayo 2 Super open reasoning model for autonomous vehicles
bullets.body: Jensen Huang announced the commercial launch of Alpamayo 2 Super, described as a frontier open reasoning model designed for robotaxis and autonomous vehicles, featuring 360° awareness, high-level driving decisions, and automated reasoning labels.

bullets.title: MSFT Azure hits $100B run rate; enterprise AI moving beyond single-model dependency
bullets.body: Microsoft's Azure reached a $100B annual run rate, with one account highlighting that 'enterprise AI is moving beyond one model'—implying diversified AI workloads across the customer base. MSFT was cited as approaching a $500 price target.

bullets.title: LITE: AXTI InP substrate supply relationship detailed; FN, CIEN calls positive
bullets.body: Multiple accounts highlighted that AXTI supplies InP substrates (essential for lasers) to LITE, providing AXTI upfront funding and long-term demand visibility while LITE secures a critical input. Separately, analyst calls with FN, CIEN, and LITE all characterized these as 'great companies' with strong long-term prospects. CIEN's WaveLogic 6 remains the only 1.6T coherent system deployed at scale with a $7.8B backlog.

bullets.title: AI capex demand strong 9-12+ months; Morgan Stanley says open-weight models expand market
bullets.body: One account assessed AI capex demand as solid for at least 9-12 months, with lagging cyclicals (housing, office) expected to inflect higher and consumption to hold up on labor market resilience. Morgan Stanley separately argued open-weight models (Kimi K3, Qwen, Llama) should accelerate AI adoption by lowering costs and are unlikely to hurt industry leaders.

bullets.title: AMZN: Bezos files $4B stock sale; AWS cited as best-positioned inference cloud
bullets.body: Jeff Bezos filed to sell ~$4B in Amazon stock following a recent surge, with premarket shares down ~2%. One account separately argued AWS is the best-positioned inference cloud provider, and another cited AMZN's multi-billion dollar North Carolina data center investment as evidence of AI infrastructure conviction.

bullets.title: Tech sector forward P/E at ~20x, near year lows and below 10-year avg of 23x
bullets.body: Bespoke noted the tech sector forward P/E ratio is approximately 20x, near the lowest level of the year and below the 10-year historical average of 23x—suggesting valuation compression despite the rally.

bullets.title: SK Hynix and SanDisk release first OCP High Bandwidth Flash spec at FMS 2026
bullets.body: SK Hynix and SanDisk jointly released the first OCP High Bandwidth Flash specification at Flash Memory Summit 2026. One account noted agentic AI will require an 'entirely new approach to storage' and that FMS this week is expected to feature significant AI storage news, with storage beginning to 'behave more like memory' as GPUs access SSDs directly in microseconds for long-context inference.

bullets.title: Macro: JOLTS misses at 7.359M, core factory orders plunge; durable goods beat
bullets.body: JOLTS job openings came in at 7.359M vs. 7.454M consensus and down from 7.594M prior, while core factory orders fell by the most in a year. Durable goods orders beat at 0.5% vs. 0.3% expected. Atlanta Fed GDPNow fell to 5.86% from 6.18%, far above the average bank Q3 GDP forecast of 2.0%.

bullets.title: Fed's Paulson: not a close call to hold; will act if inflation progress stalls
bullets.body: Philadelphia Fed President Paulson said the decision to hold rates was 'not a close call,' current policy is 'mildly restrictive,' and the Fed will need to act if progress on inflation is not made. Bessent's dovish lean was noted: his messaging shifted from 'cut rates' in January to 'don't hike' in August, signaling a less dovish stance than earlier this year.

bullets.title: SocGen sees S&P 500 at 8,000; SPX at ATH with 86% earnings beat rate and record 16.7% margins
bullets.body: Societe Generale upgraded its S&P 500 target to 8,000, citing 86% earnings beat rate, record profit margins of 16.7%, and broadening strength beyond Big Tech. The S&P 500 hit a new intraday all-time high during the session—a fast round-trip from one-month closing low to ATH in just four sessions. SocGen's message: 'buy the dip.'

bullets.title: GLW: Trump administration drafting polysilicon price floor and new tariffs to protect Hemlock
bullets.body: The Trump administration is preparing a price floor on polysilicon and new tariffs on polysilicon and derivative products used in chips and solar panels. The move aims to protect U.S. producers including Hemlock Semiconductor, which is majority-owned by Corning.
